clue.text: Parrot circling an overhanging shelter

indicators.note: circling means the first piece goes round the second

parts.note: to parrot is to copy or mimic

explanation.surface: A pet parrot flies around a covered awning in the garden.
explanation.definitionFit: A canopy is a cover hanging over a bed, throne or doorway, giving protection from above.

clue.text: Copy-editor number one upset by writing fee

parts.note: a sub, short for sub-editor, prepares copy for print
a script is a piece of writing

indicators.note: upset in a down-the-page sense turns the pair number-one over so it reads the other way

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: The chief copy-editor is annoyed by a charge for writing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' turns NO + I into ION; 'by' just sets SCRIPT beside the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A subscription is a regular payment charged for membership or a periodical.

clue.text: Put off deciding what to do with bed

definitions.meaning: to delay a decision until the next day
literally, lie down on a bed and rest

explanation.surface: Procrastinating over what to do with a bed.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means postpone a choice overnight; read literally, it is what a bed is for.

clue.text: Irregular discolouration left in cowboy builder's work

indicators.note: in means one piece is placed inside the other

parts.note: a cowboy builder is a shoddy, untrustworthy tradesman, whose work is a botch

explanation.surface: A stain is all that is left by a dodgy builder's job.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'cowboy builder' is British slang for an incompetent or dishonest tradesman.
explanation.definitionFit: A blotch is a patchy mark or stain on a surface or skin.

clue.text: Percentage rise ordered to cover area hotel employees

parts.note: a commission is a percentage of a sale paid to an agent

indicators.note: ordered means the letters are put into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Hotel staff are told their percentage pay will rise across the area.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to cover' only joins the anagram fodder: RISE and A are rearranged together into AIRES.
explanation.definitionFit: Commissionaires are uniformed doormen at hotels, cinemas and offices.

clue.text: Trendy agent's shown up to meet lad face to face

parts.note: in means fashionable

indicators.note: shown up in a down entry means written bottom to top, so read backwards

parts.note: a rep, short for representative, is a sales agent; the 's is a link
a son is a boy or lad

explanation.surface: A fashionable agent appears to meet a young man in the flesh.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something in person means being physically present, meeting directly.

clue.text: Pinching the paper

parts.note: FT is the Financial Times, a British newspaper

explanation.surface: Someone is stealing the newspaper.
explanation.definitionFit: Pinching is informal for stealing, the act of taking another's property.

clue.text: Lavishness of couple rebuilding to house small unit for printing

indicators.note: to house means to contain the other piece
rebuilding means these letters are reassembled in a new order

parts.note: an en is a printer's unit of width, half an em

explanation.surface: A couple renovating their home to fit a small printing unit live lavishly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rebuilding' gives OPULCE, and 'to house' wraps it round the printer's unit; 'couple' looks like a pair of people but is only fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Opulence is great wealth or luxury, so lavishness in display or living.

clue.text: Large number have a complaint when It goes astray

definitions.text: Large number have a complaint when It goes astray

parts.note: M is the Roman numeral for a thousand
to ail is to be unwell, to suffer a complaint

explanation.surface: Many people grumble when the post goes missing.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines too: 'It' stands for the answer, the thing many complain about when lost.
explanation.definitionFit: Post that is lost in delivery brings many complaints from senders and recipients.

clue.text: Disposed of what was left after liquidation

definitions.meaning: dealt with the remaining opposition or tasks
wiped with a cloth after liquid was spilt

explanation.surface: Clearing away the remains after a business is liquidated.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb means finishing off remnants, and also soaking up a spill with a mop.

clue.text: Greek character returning after short time offers driving force

parts.note: a moment is a brief period

indicators.note: returning means this piece reads backwards

parts.note: mu is a letter of the Greek alphabet

explanation.surface: A Greek returning after a brief spell brings impetus.
explanation.definitionFit: Momentum is the impetus that keeps something moving forward.

clue.text: Went round — no answer — went off

indicators.note: no means the following letter is left out

parts.note: rotated means turned or went round

explanation.surface: Someone spun round, gave no reply, and left.
explanation.definitionFit: Food that has gone off has decayed or spoiled.

clue.text: Posh tie, shy, dressed up to make proposition

indicators.note: dressed up suggests rearranging the fodder like smartening up clothes

explanation.surface: A posh tie on a shy man, all dressed up, makes a suggestion.
explanation.definitionFit: A hypothesis is a proposed explanation put forward for testing.

clue.text: On holiday, with reserve in place of business

parts.note: off means away from work
ice means reserve or coolness of manner

explanation.surface: A holidaymaker keeps a reserve at their workplace.
explanation.definitionFit: An office is a room or building where business is carried on.

clue.text: Self-employed fencer with ale being spilt

indicators.note: being spilt suggests the letters splash about into a new order

explanation.surface: A self-employed swordsman spills his beer.
explanation.definitionFit: A freelance works independently for several clients rather than one employer.

clue.text: Staged a party and gave it a go

definitions.meaning: a bash is informal for a party
to have a bash is to attempt something

explanation.surface: Someone threw a party and tried their luck.
explanation.definitionFit: The informal phrase means both threw a celebration and made an attempt.

clue.text: Outbuilding accommodating single wee Scot?

indicators.note: accommodating means holding the other piece inside

parts.note: a barn is a farm outbuilding
I is the Roman numeral one, a single

explanation.surface: A barn houses a single small Scotsman.
explanation.definitionFit: Bairn is the Scottish word for a child, a little Scot.

clue.text: Supports leg movement achieved by some potters

parts.note: backs means supports
pin is slang for a leg

explanation.surface: Pottery makers use their leg to work the wheel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'potters' are snooker players potting balls, not makers of pots.
explanation.definitionFit: Backspin is reverse rotation put on a ball, as snooker players do to make it screw back.

clue.text: Smart hat more than covers Mary's sister

indicators.note: the two words together more than cover the name, holding it within them

explanation.surface: A smart hat does more than cover a woman's head.
explanation.definitionFit: In the Gospels, Martha is the sister of Mary and Lazarus of Bethany.

clue.text: Study complaint in this French place where cross-country runners meet

parts.note: to con is to study or learn
flu is an illness or complaint
en is French for in
ce is French for this

explanation.surface: A study of an illness at a cross-country race venue in France.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'runners' are rivers running across country.
explanation.definitionFit: A confluence is the junction where two rivers flow together.

clue.text: Affectedly superior boy and girl

parts.note: a lad is a boy
Ida is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A snooty young couple.
explanation.definitionFit: La-di-da describes pretentious, posh manners or speech.

clue.text: Dicey, showing sign of hesitation leaving court

indicators.note: leaving means these letters depart from the other word

parts.note: Chancery is a division of the English High Court
er is the sound of hesitating

explanation.surface: A risky moment as a hesitant person walks out of court.
explanation.definitionFit: Chancy is informal for risky or uncertain, much like dicey.

clue.text: Rose crazy to come back with invite

indicators.note: to come back means this word is read in reverse

parts.note: mad means crazy
to ask is to invite

explanation.surface: Someone got up, mad to return with an invitation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rose' looks like a verb but is the flower.
explanation.definitionFit: The damask is a fragrant old variety of rose, originally from Damascus.

clue.text: Base silver starts shining

parts.note: Ag is the chemical symbol for silver
low means base or mean

explanation.surface: A base of silver begins to gleam.
explanation.definitionFit: Aglow means glowing, giving off a warm light.

clue.text: Subcontinental graduate's entered ship

indicators.note: entered means going inside the other piece

parts.note: an Indian is from the Indian subcontinent
an MA is a Master of Arts graduate; the 's is a link

explanation.surface: A graduate from India boards a vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: An Indiaman was a large merchant ship trading with India, like those of the East India Company.

clue.text: Go to collect everything for each one making rapid progress

indicators.note: to collect means gather the other piece inside

parts.note: taken as written
all means everything
per means for each

explanation.surface: Someone goes round gathering everything for each person, at speed.
explanation.definitionFit: A galloper is a horse or rider at full gallop, moving fast.

clue.text: Prepare to shoot bird

definitions.meaning: to pull back a gun's hammer ready for firing

explanation.surface: Readying a gun to fire at a bird.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means raising a gun's hammer, and also a male chicken.

clue.text: Echoes of swan in flight appear

indicators.note: in flight suggests the letters scatter and fly into a new order

explanation.surface: The calls of a swan as it flies appear in the air.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to turn up or be seen somewhere, to make an appearance.
